Dated : 11th June, 2024 P.C:-
1.

The present Writ Petition is fled by the Petitioners for quashing and setting aside of the proceedings in POCSO Special Case No. 28 of 2018 arsing out of C.R. No. 311 of 2017 registered with Mahim Police Station, the same being null and void.
Pending the hearing and fnal disposal of the Petition, it was also prayed that the proceedings in POCSO Special Case be stayed.

sentences.text: As per the said request, on 09.10.2019, while issuing notice to the complainant, by referring to the report of the Probation Offcer, Unit 5, dated 15.11.2017 and the complainant's statement under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1963, the Division Bench directed that no charge shall be framed in the subject crime till the next date and this order is continued from time to time.

2. We have heard the learned counsel, Mr. Pradhan appearing for the Petitioners (Original Accused Nos.1 and 2), the learned APP, Ms Deshmukh for the Respondent/State and the learned counsel, Ms Gond representing the complainant/Respondent No. 2.
The Petitioners are the husband and wife and the Respondent No. 2 is their niece.

On 25.10.2017 the Respondent No. 2 approached Mahim Police Station, accusing that the accused No. 1 was sexually abusing her since she was 6 to 7 years old and this continued till she attained age of 13 years.
She complained that despite being married, he continued to sexually abuse her and used to threaten her and beat her if she did not cooperate.
Being fed-up of this attitude, she narrated the incident to her aunt six months back who did not believe her version and burnt her hands by candle, which forced her to keep mum.

Unable to bear the torture, she attempted to commit suicide but when once again on 22.10.2016, while she was subjected to sexual abuse, she approached the police station which resulted in registration of an offence by invoking Section 376(2), 323, R.V.Patil 3/5 14 WP.5729.2018.odt 324, 506 of the Indian Penal Code as well as the Provisions of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO)
Act, 2012

sentences.text: as in the complaint she stated that she was 16 years old.

3. When the Respondent No.2 was sent to the Child Welfare Committee on 15.11.2017 her statement was recorded, where she divulged that she was in love with one boy and when this was made known to her relatives including her uncle and her father, restrictions were put on her movements and she was permitted to appear for her Class 10th examination privately.

She categorically stated that when her uncle and aunt came to know about her affair, they also curtailed her movement and therefore on 25.10.2017 she went to the police station and lodged a report by giving false information.

Even in her statement recorded before the Magistrate on 01.11.2017, she reiterated her stand and stated, that she used to like a boy and when she oppressed her family members about this, her uncle slapped her.
One day when he had beaten her excessively, she decided to approach the police station and lodged a false complaint, as she intended to teach a lesson to them.

4. The learned counsel, Mr. Pradhan has invited our attention to the orders passed on the Bail Applications fled by both the accused persons i.e. on 14.6.2018 and 28.08.2018, when by referring Mohd. sentences.text: Apart from this, Mr. Pradhan submit that since the year 2019 the proceedings in the POCSO Special Case No.28 of 2017 have been stayed.

5. The learned counsel for the Respondent No. 2 has fled an affdavit wherein she has categorically stated that in a ft of anger she had lodged the complaint against the Petitioners which has resulted into a POCSO Special Case which is pending before the Special Judge for Greater Mumbai.
She categorically has deposed that she used to like a boy in the neighborhood but her family members did not approve of her relationship with him and imposed restrictions on her movements.
In order to revenge, she decided to lodge a false FIR so as to teach lesson to her uncle and her aunt with whom she was staying.

In the later part of the affdavit she has categorically stated that she got married to the said boy with whom she was courting on 30.04.2021 and out of the wedlock her daughter is born and she is residing happily with her husband and sharing a family warm.
6. This is a ft case for quashing the proceedings though the learned APP, Ms Deshmukh would vehemently oppose the same by submitting that the Respondent No. 2 has abused the process of law.

It may hold true but in any case continuing the criminal proceedings against the Petitioners would rather amount to abuse of process of law, as in her statement under Section 164 as well as in the statement given to the Probation R.V.Patil 5/5 14 WP.5729.2018.odt Offcer, the Respondent No.
2 has categorically admitted that in order to tackle with the opposition which she faced at the instance of her uncle and aunt i.e. the present Petitioners, she had lodged a false FIR.

In any case continuation of the proceedings against the Petitioners would be just a rigmarole to be followed as the Respondent No. 2 in the affdavit fled, has categorically stated that she has no intention to continue with the proceedings as she is happily leading her life.

Forcing her to depose before the Court and with every possibility that she will stuck-up to her stand which she had maintained in her 164 statement, would ultimately result in the Petitioners being acquitted and would be a gross abuse of process of law.

For this aforesaid reason, we deem it appropriate to allow the Writ Petition in terms of prayer clause (a) is as under:
"(a) A Writ of Certiorari or any other appropriate writ, order or direction in the like nature be issued thereby declaring the entire proceedings in POCSO Special Case No.
28 of 2018 arising out of C.R. No. 311 of 2017 registered at Mahim Police Station, as illegal, null and void and hence be quashed and set aside and the Petitioners /
Original Accused Nos. 1 and 2 be discharged therefrom."
No orders as to costs.
